output.myth: Storm-petrels nest in the cracks of the north cliff, where no fox can reach, and their chicks are dark and quiet. Old Hesk the Reel counted them every autumn with a knot in her cord. One year Tavo the Gale came up the cliff in a black wind and tore the nest open, and the chicks went up the wind like sparks off a fire. Hesk counted and found one short. The last was the smallest and had not learned to fly. Aun saw it turning above the rocks. He had already cut one string and did not want to cut another, so he lit the lamp from his own kite and gave it to the chick. Now the chicks glow when they fly, and they say if you see a soft cluster of lights over the cliff in a gale, it is the nest still counting. Mirath is the last one, the one that was short.
output.verse:
Lamps in the cliff-crack,
the last chick still counts the wind,
one soft light comes home.
